column2: Retain Egypt’s forces like seashore sand, many ships and the deceitful plan to absorb Alexander’s kingdom. The simile and annexation motive remain explicit.
Retain peaceful words, city receptions and Alexander’s instruction based on the father-in-law relationship. The outward welcome is not used to erase the narrated deceit.
Retain Ptolemy stationing a garrison in each entered city. Each marks repeated local occupation, not merely one central garrison.

Retain burned Dagon temple, ruined towns, bodies and heaps along the route. Jonathan is the inherited contextual subject of burning; the source does not name him in this unit until the following report.
Retain the report’s purpose of blaming Jonathan and the king’s silence. Silence is not translated as either approval or acquittal.
Retain Jonathan’s honourable reception at Joppa, mutual greeting and lodging. Lodged is the contextual overnight sense, without implying death from the sleep verb.
Retain accompaniment to the river named Eleutherus and return to Jerusalem. No modern river identification is inserted.
Retain coastal control to Seleucia by the sea and evil plans concerning Alexander. The location qualifier distinguishes the named Seleucia without supplying an alternative historical title.
Retain the proposed covenant, daughter formerly with Alexander and Demetrius’s father’s kingdom. The human diplomatic covenant does not require divine-address pronouns.
Retain regret and the claim that Alexander sought to kill him. The allegation stays inside Ptolemy’s speech.
Retain accusation because of desire for the kingdom. The narrator supplies a motive distinct from the king’s alleged attempted-murder justification.
column3: The English repeated he/him/his is difficult: Ptolemy is contextually the accuser desiring Alexander’s realm. A future literary pass should assess whether naming those referents is needed.

column2: Retain removal of the daughter, marriage transfer to Demetrius, estrangement and manifest hostility. No consent or additional ceremony is supplied.
Retain Antioch and two diadems, of Egypt and Asia, on Ptolemy’s head. The doubled crown description must not become one composite title.
Retain Alexander in Cilicia because local people were revolting. The setting gives his absence a stated cause without specifying the revolt’s leader.
Retain Alexander’s attack and Ptolemy’s counteradvance with strong force and rout. Force is contextual for strong hand; no troop count is added.
Retain flight to Arabia for shelter and Ptolemy’s exaltation. The contrast does not imply that Alexander had already been killed.
Retain Zabdiel the Arab cutting off Alexander’s head and sending it to Ptolemy. The violent action and named agent remain unsoftened.
Retain Ptolemy’s third-day death and men in strongholds destroyed by those in strongholds. Do not solve the repeated location phrase by inventing separate named factions.
column3: Which residents or garrison members are distinguished by the two groups, and from what event is the third day counted? Both remain contextual questions.

column2: Retain Demetrius’s kingship in year 167 without conversion or chronology repair.
Retain Judean mobilization against Jerusalem’s citadel and many engines. The fortification remains distinct from the holy sanctuary.
Retain lawless accusers’ hatred of their own nation and report of the siege. The moral description is the narrator’s, not a new translator label.
Retain repeated hearing, anger, immediate journey, order to stop siege and urgent meeting at Ptolemais. The repetition is source-present and need not be silently collapsed.
Retain Jonathan ordering continued siege, selecting elders/priests and exposing himself to danger. His action contrasts with the stop order and must not be rewritten as compliance.
Retain silver, gold, clothing, further gifts and finding favour. The objects are not reduced to a single unstated cash payment.
Retain some lawless men from the nation petitioning against him. Some preserves the limited indefinite group.
Retain treatment like predecessors and exaltation before all Friends. The comparison concerns Jonathan’s treatment, not universal continuity of royal policy.
Retain high priesthood and prior honours; rank among First Friends remains provisional for the final leadership/ranking infinitive.
column3: Does the infinitive make Jonathan a leader of the First Friends rather than simply a member of their rank? The inherited wording is not treated as a settled title translation.

column2: Retain Judea, three districts and Samaria in the petition, and three hundred talents promised. Do not replace the coordination with a geographically smoother reconstruction.
column3: How does Samaria relate to the three districts in this request? The later letter informs context but does not justify silently changing this syntax.

column2: Retain royal consent and letters about all these matters. Consent is not evidence that every later promise was carried out.
Retain greeting to brother Jonathan and the Jewish nation. Brother is diplomatic address, not an asserted genealogy.
Retain the copied letter to Lasthenes our Kinsman and its informational purpose. Kinsman remains a provisional court title.
Retain the nested greeting to Lasthenes his father. Father is not silently changed to adviser or a biological assertion.
column3: What honorific relationship does father express beside Kinsman? The titles need institutional review rather than a genealogical inference.

column2: Retain the decision to benefit Jewish friends for obligations kept and goodwill. Both grounds remain in the royal rationale.
Retain Judea, Aphairema/Lydda/Rathamin, attached territory, Jerusalem sacrificers and former royal dues from crops/fruit trees. The long fiscal relation remains provisional.
column3: How do the beneficiaries and in-place-of royal dues attach to the territorial confirmation? Do not treat this draft as a resolved tax assessment.

column2: Retain repeated belonging to us, tithes, dues, salt lakes and crown payments, all granted to them. Salt lakes follows the selected concrete noun rather than substituting the salt charge of chapter 10.
Retain not one provision annulled from now for all time. The emphatic negative and duration are the letter’s promise, not a guarantee by the translator.
Retain making a copy, giving it to Jonathan and conspicuous display on the holy mountain. The source’s public preservation instructions remain.
Retain quiet land, demobilization of each soldier except recruited foreigners and hostility of ancestral forces. The exception distinguishes the groups rather than all troops being discharged.
Retain Tryphon’s former Alexander affiliation, troop grumbling, Imalcue the Arab and the young Antiochus in his care. The child is Alexander’s son, not the earlier Antiochus king.
Retain persistent request to hand over the boy for kingship, reports of Demetrius and a stay of many days. Urging naturally expresses the sustained attendance in this context.
Retain Jonathan’s request to remove citadel/fortress men because they fought Israel. The two locations remain rather than reducing the request to one garrison.
Retain not only these acts but great honour for Jonathan/nation, conditioned on opportunity. The qualification must not disappear into an immediate unconditional promise.
Retain request for allied fighters because all his forces revolted. All is the king’s speech and is not harmonized with earlier foreign-troop exceptions.
Retain three thousand mighty men sent to Antioch and royal gladness at arrival. The count and destination remain exact.
Retain about one hundred twenty thousand city men intending to kill the king. The approximate large number is not reduced for historical plausibility.
Retain royal flight to the palace and inhabitants controlling passageways before fighting. Palace is contextual for court, not a detailed architectural identification.

Retain the call for Jewish help, their collective gathering/dispersal through the city and about one hundred thousand killed. The narrator’s casualty claim is preserved, not endorsed by independent historical verification.
Retain burning the city, much plunder and saving the king. The destruction is not omitted merely because the action rescues the royal figure.
Retain city people recognizing Jewish control at will, losing courage and pleading. Lost courage naturally expresses weakened minds in this military setting.
Retain the request for a right-hand pledge and cessation of fighting people/city. The embodied treaty gesture remains audible.
Retain discarded weapons, peace, Jewish honour before king/kingdom and return with spoils. The initial peace-making subject is distinct from the subsequent honoured group.
Retain enthroned Demetrius and the land quiet before him. No duration beyond the source statement is supplied.
Retain all promises proved false, estrangement, unreturned goodwill and severe oppression. The repeated reciprocal goodwill relation is naturally unfolded without excusing the breach.
Retain Tryphon’s return with young Antiochus, and Antiochus as the contextual enthroned subject. The named English resolution prevents attributing the child’s coronation to Tryphon here.
Retain dismissed troops gathering to Antiochus and fighting Demetrius, who fled and was routed. The English name resolves the source’s repeated pronouns contextually.
Retain Tryphon taking elephants and Antioch. Elephants interprets the beasts from the military context, not a newly supplied count.
Retain young Antiochus confirming priesthood, four districts and royal friendship. Four must not be harmonized to the three districts in earlier clauses.
Retain gold vessels, table service and permission for gold drinking vessels, purple and golden clasp. Table service for the service noun remains a provisional material interpretation.
column3: Does service mean table equipment, attendants or another court provision here? Gold vessels alone do not settle the second item.

column2: Retain Simon’s command from the Ladder of Tyre to Egypt’s borders. The geographical title remains untranslated as a modern location claim.
Retain Beyond the River, city travel, all Syrian forces joining and Ascalon’s honourable reception. The regional expression is not silently assigned a newly named river.
Retain Gaza’s refusal, siege and burning/plunder of surrounding towns. The victims’ locality is distinct from an expressly completed burning of Gaza itself.
Retain appeal, right-hand pledge, rulers’ sons as hostages sent to Jerusalem and passage to Damascus. The pledge does not erase the hostage requirement.
Retain Demetrius’s commanders at Kedesh in Galilee intending to remove Jonathan from office. Office is contextual for the service/responsibility term and not an explicitly named priesthood here.
Retain Jonathan meeting them while Simon remains in the country. The division of roles prepares the separate Beth-zur action.
Retain Simon’s prolonged Beth-zur attack and blockade. The final enclosure is not merely another synonym for marching there.

Propose They asked him for his right hand in pledge, and he gave it to them. This clarifies that the petitioners receive the pledge and restores the bodily idiom; inherited asked him to receive can reverse that relation. Keep their expulsion, city capture and new garrison.
Retain Gennesar water, early departure and Hazor’s plain. No unstated lake designation or modern route is necessary in the text.
Propose restoring Behold before the foreign army’s encounter. Preserve the mountain ambush and frontal approach as distinct tactical actions.
Retain the ambush group rising from its positions and joining battle. Men naturally unfolds the collective ambush noun.
Retain all fleeing with exactly two named exceptions, Mattathias son of Absalom and Judas son of Chalphi. The exception is explicit and neither figure is conflated with earlier famous namesakes.
Retain torn clothes, earth on head and prayer. The prayer’s words are not supplied because none are recorded.
Retain return to battle, rout and enemy flight. The unexpressed singular subject contextually resumes Jonathan without inventing a divine intervention clause.
Retain former fugitives returning to Jonathan and pursuing to Kedesh/the enemy camp, then camping there. The two camp references need not identify the same original base as Jonathan’s.
Retain about three thousand foreigners fallen and Jonathan’s return to Jerusalem. The approximate tally is preserved without reconciling it to another battle.
